findings.xr: Multiple rounded mineralized loose bodies in a distended joint; pressure erosions may be present.
findings.ct: Numerous calcified or ossified intra-articular bodies, with better definition of mineralization and erosions.
findings.mri: Lobulated synovial proliferation with multiple low-signal loose bodies; cartilage nodules are typically T2 bright.

findings.xr: Often occult; may show soft-tissue swelling, joint-space loss, or erosions in chronic inflammatory disease.
findings.ct: Numerous small, uniform filling bodies within distended synovium; useful for calcification and osseous change.
findings.mri: Numerous small, ovoid low-signal bodies in distended synovium or bursa, commonly with synovitis and enhancement.

pathologies.name: PVNS / diffuse-type tenosynovial giant cell tumor

findings.xr: Usually normal or shows a joint effusion and pressure erosions without matrix mineralization.
findings.ct: Soft-tissue synovial mass with erosions; CT can show high attenuation from hemosiderin.
findings.mri: Lobulated synovial mass with low signal on T1/T2 and blooming on gradient-echo or susceptibility sequences.

findings.xr: Chronic joint effusion with nonspecific soft-tissue fullness; degenerative changes may coexist.
findings.ct: Fat-density frond-like synovial proliferation within a joint or bursa.
findings.mri: Frond-like fatty synovial mass: high T1 and T2 signal that suppresses on fat-suppressed sequences, with effusion.

findings.xr: Eccentric punched-out erosions with overhanging edges, preserved joint space early, and soft-tissue tophi.
findings.ct: Hyperdense tophaceous deposits with erosions; dual-energy CT can identify urate deposition.
findings.mri: Variable-signal tophus with low-to-intermediate T1 signal, variable T2 signal, enhancement, and erosions.

findings.xr: Linear or punctate cartilage and fibrocartilage calcification, atypical osteoarthritis distribution, or hook osteophytes.
findings.ct: Thin calcific deposits in cartilage, fibrocartilage, tendons, or ligaments; CT is sensitive for subtle calcification.
findings.mri: Often limited for calcification; low-signal cartilage deposits and degenerative or inflammatory changes may be seen.

findings.xr: Amorphous, homogeneous peri-tendinous calcification, often adjacent to the greater tuberosity or around the hip.
findings.ct: Dense amorphous hydroxyapatite deposit with precise anatomic localization and possible cortical erosion.
findings.mri: Low-signal calcific focus with surrounding edema, bursitis, tendon inflammation, or a resorptive phase reaction.

findings.xr: Rapidly destructive rotator cuff arthropathy with superior humeral migration, joint-space loss, and large effusion.
findings.ct: Advanced cuff-tear arthropathy with destructive osseous change and joint debris; calcific deposits may be present.
findings.mri: Massive cuff tear, large joint effusion, synovitis, cartilage loss, and destructive changes in a characteristic elderly patient.

findings.xr: Periarticular osteopenia, cystic erosions, joint-space narrowing, or shoulder-pad soft-tissue fullness.
findings.ct: Periarticular soft-tissue thickening and erosive or cystic change, often in dialysis-related disease.
findings.mri: Nodular synovial thickening and low-signal deposits, with erosions or large effusions; may mimic inflammatory arthropathy.

findings.xr: Joint-space narrowing, epiphyseal overgrowth, widened intercondylar notch, subchondral cysts, and hemosiderin-related density.
findings.ct: Chronic arthropathy with erosions, cysts, osteophytes, and high-density blood products or synovium.
findings.mri: Hemosiderin-laden hypertrophic synovium with low-signal blooming, recurrent blood products, cartilage loss, and cysts.

findings.xr: The six D's: distention, density, debris, disorganization, dislocation, and destruction; midfoot collapse is classic.
findings.ct: Three-dimensional depiction of fragmentation, subluxation, fractures, rocker-bottom deformity, and osseous debris.
findings.mri: Marrow edema, fractures, joint destruction, and soft-tissue change; distribution and clinical context help separate infection.

findings.xr: Phemister triad: juxta-articular osteopenia, peripheral osseous erosions, and gradual joint-space narrowing.
findings.ct: Erosions, abscesses, synovial thickening, and calcified nodes or collections may be demonstrated.
findings.mri: Large joint effusion with synovitis, erosions, marrow edema, and rim-enhancing abscesses; rice bodies can occur.

findings.xr: Small radiolucent nidus with surrounding dense reactive sclerosis, often subtle in the spine or cancellous bone.
findings.ct: Best test for a tiny lucent nidus, sometimes with central mineralization, surrounded by reactive sclerosis.
findings.mri: Extensive marrow and soft-tissue edema may obscure the nidus; enhancement and synovitis can accompany an intra-articular lesion.

findings.xr: Well-defined geographic lytic epiphyseal lesion with a thin sclerotic rim; stippled calcification may be present.
findings.ct: Shows the epiphyseal lesion, matrix mineralization, cortical integrity, and possible secondary aneurysmal change.
findings.mri: T2-variable lobulated lesion with edema, enhancement, joint effusion, and possible fluid-fluid levels.

findings.xr: Expansile lytic epiphyseal-metaphyseal lesion extending to the subchondral bone, usually without a sclerotic rim.
findings.ct: Defines cortical thinning, breakthrough, matrix absence, and pathologic fracture.
findings.mri: Heterogeneous low-to-intermediate T2 signal with solid enhancement, cortical breach, soft-tissue component, and fluid-fluid levels if secondary ABC.

findings.xr: Expansile, eccentric, lucent metaphyseal lesion with a thin shell of bone and internal septations.
findings.ct: Expansile lytic lesion with a thin cortex, septa, and fluid-fluid levels; shows matrix or mineralized components well.
findings.mri: Multiloculated expansile lesion with multiple fluid-fluid levels, thin enhancing septa, and surrounding edema.

findings.xr: Aggressive lytic lesion with wide zone of transition, cortical destruction, and aggressive periosteal reaction.
findings.ct: Destructive lesion with soft-tissue extension and possible mineralized osteoid; helps target solid components.
findings.mri: Predominantly blood-filled or cystic mass with fluid-fluid levels but enhancing nodular solid tissue and aggressive margins.

findings.xr: Aggressive metaphyseal lesion with cloud-like osteoid, sunburst periosteal reaction, and a Codman triangle.
findings.ct: Characterizes mineralized osteoid, cortical destruction, and extraosseous mineralization.
findings.mri: T1-low, heterogeneous mass with marrow and soft-tissue extension; shows neurovascular relationships and skip lesions.

findings.xr: Dense ossified surface-based mass attached to cortex, often on the posterior distal femur, with a cleavage plane.
findings.ct: Dense juxtacortical osteoid mass with cortical involvement and possible medullary extension; CT maps anatomy well.
findings.mri: Low-signal mineralized mass with variable higher-signal cartilaginous areas, soft-tissue extension, and medullary involvement.

findings.xr: Surface-based chondroid or osteoid mass with cortical saucerization and perpendicular periosteal reaction.
findings.ct: Cortical saucerization, surface mineralization, and subtle medullary involvement are well shown.
findings.mri: Lobulated surface mass with cortical involvement, heterogeneous signal, and adjacent marrow or soft-tissue extension.

xr.caption: There is a broad based eccentric lytic lesion in the diaphysis of the right midshaft of femur involving the lateral cortex with periosteal reaction. There is also evidence of thickening of the adjacent cortex. Soft tissue opacity mass is seen anteriorly, suggesting an extraosseous soft tissue component.

findings.xr: Small well-defined juxtacortical lucent lesion causing saucer-like cortical scalloping, often with a sclerotic rim and stippled calcification.
findings.ct: Lobulated surface-based cartilage lesion with cortical saucerization and chondroid mineralization, usually without medullary invasion.
findings.mri: Lobulated T2-bright cartilage mass with cortical scalloping and peripheral or septal enhancement; marrow and soft-tissue extension are absent or limited.

findings.xr: Exophytic sessile or pedunculated lesion with uninterrupted cortical and medullary continuity with the parent bone.
findings.ct: Confirms corticomedullary continuity and detects complications such as fracture, neurovascular impingement, or bursitis.
findings.mri: Cartilage cap is high T2 signal; cap thickness and nodular enhancement are assessed when malignant transformation is suspected.

findings.xr: Central medullary lucent lesion with chondroid rings-and-arcs calcification, endosteal scalloping, and narrow transition.
findings.ct: Best depicts chondroid matrix mineralization and cortical scalloping or breakthrough.
findings.mri: Lobulated T2-bright cartilage lesion with septal enhancement; absence of aggressive features supports benignity.

findings.xr: Aggressive expansile lesion with rings-and-arcs mineralization, deep endosteal scalloping, cortical destruction, or soft-tissue mass.
findings.ct: Shows matrix mineralization, cortical breach, deep scalloping, and extraosseous extension.
findings.mri: Large lobulated T2-bright mass with septal and peripheral enhancement, marrow replacement, and soft-tissue extension.

findings.xr: Geographic lytic epiphyseal lesion, often with a narrow transition and variable chondroid mineralization.
findings.ct: Defines epiphyseal location, cortical integrity, and subtle matrix mineralization.
findings.mri: Lobulated T2-bright epiphyseal mass with heterogeneous enhancement and possible edema or soft-tissue extension.

findings.xr: Ground-glass matrix, hazy margins, cortical thinning, and expansion; shepherd's crook deformity can occur in the proximal femur.
findings.ct: Classic ground-glass matrix and lesion extent are best appreciated on CT; look for cortical thinning and deformity.
findings.mri: Variable T2 signal with avid enhancement; MRI is useful for complications but can look more aggressive than the radiograph.

findings.xr: Central metaphyseal lucency with a thin sclerotic margin; a fallen cortical fragment indicates fracture through the cyst.
findings.ct: Shows a simple fluid-density, centrally located lesion with cortical thinning and fracture detail.
findings.mri: Fluid-signal lesion with thin rim enhancement; fluid-fluid levels suggest hemorrhage or secondary ABC change.

findings.xr: Eccentric cortically based metaphyseal lucency with a scalloped sclerotic margin.
findings.ct: Confirms cortical origin, lesion extent, and fracture risk.
findings.mri: Variable low-to-intermediate T2 signal with a low-signal rim and variable enhancement; often more conspicuous than on radiographs.

findings.xr: Punched-out lytic skull lesion, beveled edges, or vertebra plana; periosteal reaction may occur.
findings.ct: Maps lytic cortical destruction, skull beveling, and vertebral collapse.
findings.mri: Marrow-replacing enhancing lesion with soft-tissue edema or mass; vertebral collapse may have preserved disc spaces.

findings.xr: Eccentric, multiloculated lytic lesion in the anterior mid-to-distal tibial diaphysis with a soap-bubble appearance.
findings.ct: Shows cortical involvement, internal septa, and subtle mineralization or extension.
findings.mri: Multiloculated lesion with variable T2 signal, enhancing septa, cortical breach, and soft-tissue extension.

findings.xr: Midline destructive sacral mass with bone destruction and possible calcified chondroid-like matrix.
findings.ct: Lytic midline sacral lesion with sequestra, calcification, and a large presacral soft-tissue component.
findings.mri: Very T2-bright lobulated mass with low-signal septa and honeycomb enhancement; assesses neural and pelvic extension.

findings.xr: Small, well-defined mineralized surface lesion separated from the underlying cortex by a lucent cleavage plane.
findings.ct: Clarifies the corticomedullary relationship, mineralized architecture, and cortical saucerization.
findings.mri: Heterogeneous low-to-intermediate signal mineralized mass with variable enhancement and possible adjacent edema.

findings.xr: Osteochondral overgrowth arising from one side of an epiphysis, often in the ankle or knee.
findings.ct: Defines the osteochondral excrescence and its relation to the joint surface.
findings.mri: Cartilage-cap signal and epiphyseal involvement are demonstrated; may show joint impingement or deformity.

findings.xr: Soft-tissue mass; peripheral or stippled calcification is a helpful clue, especially near a joint in a young adult.
findings.ct: Heterogeneous soft-tissue mass with calcification, hemorrhage, necrosis, and possible bone erosion.
findings.mri: Heterogeneous mass with the triple sign on T2, fluid-fluid levels, septations, and multilobulated 'bowl of grapes' appearance.

findings.xr: Fibrous dysplasia lesions with adjacent soft-tissue mass; myxoma itself may be radiographically occult.
findings.ct: Ground-glass fibrous dysplasia plus a well-defined low-attenuation intramuscular mass.
findings.mri: Intramuscular myxomas are T2 bright with peripheral fat rind and variable enhancement adjacent to fibrous dysplasia.

findings.xr: Usually occult; may cause nonspecific soft-tissue fullness without mineralization.
findings.ct: Well-circumscribed low-attenuation intramuscular mass with minimal enhancement.
findings.mri: Homogeneous T1-low, T2-high mass with avid peripheral or septal enhancement and a surrounding peritumoral fat rim.

pathologies.name: Melorheostosis
pathologies.group: Dysplasias, sclerosis, infarction, and metabolic bone

findings.xr: Dense, irregular flowing cortical hyperostosis along one side of a bone: the flowing candle-wax sign.
findings.ct: Maps dense cortical hyperostosis, medullary involvement, and soft-tissue ossification.
findings.mri: Low-signal cortical sclerosis with variable marrow and soft-tissue changes; MRI can show contractures or pain generators.

pathologies.name: Osteopoikilosis
pathologies.group: Dysplasias, sclerosis, infarction, and metabolic bone

findings.xr: Multiple small, well-defined, symmetric enostoses clustered around epiphyses and carpal/tarsal bones.
findings.ct: Confirms numerous uniformly sclerotic medullary foci without aggressive features.
findings.mri: Low-signal foci on all sequences without edema or enhancement, helping distinguish incidental osteopoikilosis.

pathologies.name: Osteopathia striata
pathologies.group: Dysplasias, sclerosis, infarction, and metabolic bone

findings.xr: Linear striations of metaphyseal and diaphyseal medullary sclerosis, often bilateral and symmetric.
findings.ct: Fine longitudinal medullary sclerotic bands are demonstrated.
findings.mri: Low-signal linear bands on all sequences, generally without marrow edema or aggressive enhancement.

pathologies.name: Paget disease of bone
pathologies.group: Dysplasias, sclerosis, infarction, and metabolic bone

findings.xr: Cortical thickening, coarsened trabeculae, bone expansion, picture-frame vertebra, or cotton-wool skull.
findings.ct: Shows cortical and trabecular thickening, expansion, fissure fractures, and complications.
findings.mri: Variable marrow signal depending on phase; useful for complications such as sarcomatous transformation or stenosis.

pathologies.name: Bone infarct
pathologies.group: Dysplasias, sclerosis, infarction, and metabolic bone

findings.xr: Medullary serpiginous sclerosis with a geographic, often metaphyseal or diaphyseal distribution.
findings.ct: Peripheral serpiginous sclerosis and central fat or calcification are well characterized.
findings.mri: Serpiginous peripheral low-signal rim with the double-line sign on T2; internal fat signal is preserved in chronic stages.

pathologies.name: Osteonecrosis / AVN
pathologies.group: Dysplasias, sclerosis, infarction, and metabolic bone

findings.xr: Patchy sclerosis and lucency, flattening, and the subchondral crescent sign indicating collapse.
findings.ct: Depicts the subchondral fracture, sclerosis, collapse, and articular surface contour.
findings.mri: Band-like low-signal lesion with the T2 double-line sign, marrow edema, and assessment of bilateral or multifocal disease.

pathologies.name: Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the femoral head
pathologies.group: Dysplasias, sclerosis, infarction, and metabolic bone

findings.xr: May be normal early; later shows subchondral sclerosis, flattening, or collapse.
findings.ct: Shows a subtle subchondral fracture line, sclerosis, and articular surface collapse.
findings.mri: Irregular or serpiginous low-signal subchondral line with extensive edema; usually more distal and irregular than AVN.

pathologies.name: Transient osteoporosis of the hip
pathologies.group: Dysplasias, sclerosis, infarction, and metabolic bone

findings.xr: Often normal initially, followed by diffuse regional osteopenia without focal collapse.
findings.ct: May show diffuse osteopenia but no discrete fracture or focal necrosis.
findings.mri: Diffuse bone-marrow edema of the femoral head, neck, and sometimes acetabulum without a focal subchondral lesion.

pathologies.name: Brodie abscess
pathologies.group: Infection, trauma, and strange soft-tissue processes

findings.xr: Subacute metaphyseal lucency with a surrounding rim of sclerosis, sometimes with a serpiginous tract.
findings.ct: Shows a well-defined lytic cavity, sequestrum, sclerosis, and cortical or soft-tissue extension.
findings.mri: T1-low, T2-high intraosseous abscess with rim enhancement and the T1 penumbra sign.

pathologies.name: Chronic osteomyelitis: sequestrum / involucrum / cloaca
pathologies.group: Infection, trauma, and strange soft-tissue processes

findings.xr: Sequestrum is dense dead bone within involucrum; cloaca is a cortical drainage opening, with sclerosis and sinus tract.
findings.ct: Best depicts sequestrum, cortical cloaca, involucrum, sinus tracts, and surgical anatomy.
findings.mri: Marrow replacement and enhancement with abscess or sinus tract; sequestrum remains low signal and nonenhancing.

pathologies.name: Myositis ossificans
pathologies.group: Infection, trauma, and strange soft-tissue processes

findings.xr: Peripheral mature ossification with a lucent center: the zonal phenomenon, often separated from adjacent cortex.
findings.ct: Rim-predominant mineralization, zonal maturation, and cortical separation are clearly shown.
findings.mri: Early lesion can be T2 bright and edematous; peripheral low-signal mineralization and variable enhancement mature over time.

pathologies.name: Calcific myonecrosis
pathologies.group: Infection, trauma, and strange soft-tissue processes

findings.xr: Long-segment fusiform soft-tissue calcification, usually in a muscle compartment after remote trauma or compartment syndrome.
findings.ct: Peripheral curvilinear or stippled calcification within a fusiform low-density compartment lesion.
findings.mri: Encapsulated fusiform mass with heterogeneous T1/T2 signal, peripheral low-signal rim, and little internal enhancement.

pathologies.name: Morel-Lavallée lesion
pathologies.group: Infection, trauma, and strange soft-tissue processes

findings.xr: Usually occult; may show soft-tissue swelling or dystrophic calcification in a chronic lesion.
findings.ct: Well-defined post-traumatic fluid collection between subcutaneous fat and deep fascia, sometimes with blood products or fat globules.
findings.mri: Lentiform fluid collection along the fascial plane with internal septa, debris, capsule, and variable blood-product signal.

pathologies.name: Elastofibroma dorsi
pathologies.group: Infection, trauma, and strange soft-tissue processes

findings.xr: Often occult; may show a bilateral infrascapular soft-tissue mass or subtle rib remodeling.
findings.ct: Bilateral, poorly circumscribed infrascapular masses with alternating soft-tissue and fat streaks.
findings.mri: Characteristic alternating fibrous low-signal and fat high-signal bands beneath the scapula, with variable enhancement.

pathologies.name: Diabetic muscle infarction / diabetic myonecrosis
pathologies.group: Infection, trauma, and strange soft-tissue processes

findings.xr: Usually normal or shows nonspecific soft-tissue swelling; calcification is uncommon.
findings.ct: Enlarged edematous muscle with low attenuation, perifascial fluid, and variable rim enhancement; exclude abscess.
findings.mri: Diffuse muscle enlargement and T2 hyperintensity with perifascial edema, patchy enhancement, and nonenhancing necrotic areas.

findings.xr: Periprosthetic radiolucent lines and expansile osteolysis, often with eccentric polyethylene wear, component migration, or calcar resorption.
findings.ct: Lucent periprosthetic cavities with cortical thinning or defects; metal-artifact reduction maps osteolysis, component position, and heterotopic ossification.
findings.mri: Synovial thickening or a periprosthetic mass with low-signal metal debris, marrow edema, and possible soft-tissue extension; assess for adverse local tissue reaction.
